title: 2020 Focused Updates to the Asthma Management Guidelines: A Report from the National Asthma Education and Prevention Program Coordinating Committee Expert Panel Working Group
authors: Cloutier MM, Baptist AP, Blake KV, Brooks EG, Bryant-Stephens T, DiMango E, et al.
journal: Journal of Allergy and Clinical Immunology
funder: The report was funded by the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute of the National Institutes of Health; no additional funding was received and all authors volunteered their time.
authorConflicts: Panel members disclosed personal fees, grants and non-financial support for the preceding 36 months; a member with a moderate conflict related to a topic was recused from writing, discussion and voting on it. One member with grants from Novartis, AstraZeneca, Teva and Takeda was recused from the inhaled corticosteroid recommendations; one member with personal fees from AstraZeneca and other companies was recused and withdrew in October 2019; several members with smaller industry ties were not recused.
result: For people aged 12 years and older with mild persistent asthma, the panel conditionally recommends either daily low-dose inhaled corticosteroid with as-needed short-acting beta2-agonist, or as-needed inhaled corticosteroid and short-acting beta2-agonist used concomitantly (Recommendation 10). It recommends inhaled corticosteroid-formoterol in a single inhaler as both controller and reliever for moderate to severe persistent asthma from 4 years (Recommendation 12). The panel did not address as-needed inhaled corticosteroid-formoterol against as-needed short-acting beta2-agonist in Step 1 (intermittent asthma), because the comparison was outside its key questions. Conflict management followed Institute of Medicine standards.
